payload.stem: Two carts of equal mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ at rest on a frictionless track are pushed apart by a compressed spring between them. The spring releases a total of $4\text{ J}$ of energy, which becomes kinetic energy of the carts, and the carts have equal kinetic energy because their masses are equal: $2.00\text{ J}$ each. In a second trial one of the carts is replaced by a cart with $4$ times the mass, and the spring releases the same $4\text{ J}$. What is the best prediction of the kinetic energy of the lighter cart in the second trial?

options.why: Gives the lighter cart the inverse share, $E/(1+f)$.
Gives all of the energy to the lighter cart.
Gives the lighter cart the same share as before, ignoring the larger mass of the other cart.
Momentum is conserved, so $mv_1=(4m)v_2$ and $v_1=4v_2$. The kinetic energies are in the ratio $K_1:K_2=4:1$, so the lighter cart has the fraction $4/(4+1)$ of $4\text{ J}$, which is $3.20\text{ J}$.
